pins.ds_name: UART RX (target receives; driven by probe TX/SC)
pins.cite: Raspberry Pi 3-pin Debug Connector Specification RP-003139-SP-4, p.1 Pinout table; RP-003139-SP-4 p.4 footprint figure (side entry SM03B-SRSS-TB: 1 SC, 2 GND, 3 SD; top entry: 1 UART_RX, 2 GND, 3 UART_TX); Raspberry Pi Debug Probe docs (introduction.adoc): "Orange:: TX/SC (Output from Probe) / Black:: GND / Yellow:: RX/SD (Input to Probe or I/O)"
pins.quote: "1  RX  SC" and "when talking about UART TX and RX, we are talking about these pins from the target perspective ... RX means the signal driving into the SoC"; straight-through pin 1 to pin 1 cable; probe pin 1 = "TX/SC (Output from Probe)"
pins.issue: MISMATCH: design puts UART_TX (GPIO20 = UART1 TX, RP2350 datasheet sec 1.2.3 Table 3 p.19; docs/pinmap.md "UART1 TX to J6 pin 1") on pin 1. With the straight-through Debug Probe cable the probe's TX output and the RP2354B TX output both drive pin 1 (contention, no link). Swap: pin 1 = UART_RX (GPIO21), pin 3 = UART_TX (GPIO20). PCB pads agree with design.py (battler.kicad_pcb J6 pad 1 = UART_TX).
pins.resolution: fixed: pin 1 is now UART_RX, as the debug connector spec names it from the board side
